page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.2-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 4 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The CPU incorporates modern vector capabilities including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic hardware extensions. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no discrete GPU acceleration, and does not include local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute performance alongside moderate parallel throughput. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng CPU tests, place the instance in the upper decile, driven by high per-thread efficiency and vector execution. This architecture enables high throughput in single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and text processing. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and parallel decompression place in the middle-to-lower tiers, reflecting the physical boundary of a 2-core, 4-thread virtual configuration. Memory bandwidth remains steady across cached and large-block read operations.

With its strong single-core responsiveness and moderate core footprint, the instance delivers balanced cost efficiency for lightweight to medium-concurrency workloads. It avoids the overhead of large multi-socket systems while delivering modern EPYC per-thread compute power. The instance is suited for general web serving, application middleware, API services, continuous integration build jobs, and lightweight in-memory caching such as Redis.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.2-16 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical AMD EPYC 9J45 cores clocked at 2.7 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptographic acceleration, it demonstrates top-tier single-core compute and data compression throughput. The instance provides no integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on network-attached block storage and host compute resources. While multi-core throughput is constrained by the 4-thread hardware envelope, per-thread performance is notable. The instance offers efficient resource utilization for low-to-moderate concurrency environments, making it suitable for web application hosting, microservices, Redis caching nodes, CI/CD pipeline workers, and general business logic.
